chapter: Trombonists and bandleaders across the river
title: The Johnson brothers' barbershops and the streets nearby
summary: They discuss where the brothers' barbershops were, near Newton Street and the ballrooms and clubs there.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Yeah, that's right. You see all them, both of them brothers were barbers, you know. They had barbershop there on Tash. They had barbershop right there on Tash, across the street there from that drug store. Right by Calarona drug store, across the street there.
Near Newton or where was it?
No, no, that's coming, no, that's coming this way. Up, down the river here?
Yeah, on the side of the river, on Tash. I mean down near the ferry boat here? No. Or up the river farther? No.
Oh, right on Tash, over the river. Yeah. Yeah, right on Tash Street, Nell J's here. Yeah. Right down Tash Street there.
I know, I know where Newton is and I know where the theaters and all are.
Now look, Newton, you see Newton?
Alright, that's Newton Street. Next is, uh, Deanna. Next Street, the next block. Oh yeah, just right in there.

All down there they first had business places there, ballrooms and they even had a club, a young man club there, people that upstairs had a club there too. Then down there they had two barbershops and things all that. But Yank and Buddy Jones used to cut hair, you see? Yeah.
